preconditions.expression: all(c in {'A', 'N', 'T', 'O'} for c in a)
preconditions.description: The input string `a` consists only of the characters 'A', 'N', 'T', and 'O'.
The length of `a` is between 1 and 100,000 (inclusive).
Each test case is a single line containing only the string `a`.
The first line of input is an integer `t` (1 ≤ t ≤ 100000) representing the number of test cases.

postconditions.expression: all(len(b) == len(a) for a, b in zip(test_cases, output_lines))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output string `b` has the same length as the input string `a`.

postconditions.expression: all(sorted(b) == sorted(a) for a, b in zip(test_cases, output_lines))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output string `b` is a permutation of the input string `a`.

postconditions.expression: all(all(c in {'A', 'N', 'T', 'O'} for c in b) for b in output_lines)
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output string `b` consists only of the characters 'A', 'N', 'T', and 'O'.

postconditions.expression: all(any(b == a for b in permutations(a)) for a in test_cases)
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output string `b` is a valid permutation of `a` (i.e., it is a rearrangement of the characters in `a`).

postconditions.expression: all(max_adjacent_swaps(b, a) >= max_adjacent_swaps(b2, a) for a in test_cases for b in possible_outputs(a) for b2 in possible_outputs(a) if b != b2)
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output string `b` maximizes the number of adjacent swaps required to transform `b` back to `a`. If multiple such `b` exist, any one of them is acceptable.
